text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. The most important rule is to make your code readable, as if it were a story for other humans, not just for machines. This starts with using clear naming conventions: a variable called `userAge` is far better than a mysterious `x`, and a function named `calculateTotal` explains itself immediately. Instead of writing one long, complex block, break your logic into small, focused functions that each do one job. This approach not only makes debugging easier but also boosts maintainability. When you or a teammate return to the project months later, clean code means you can understand, update, and extend it quickly without frustration. In the end, writing clean code saves time and reduces errors for everyone.
